newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight dips to 5.8/6.0 pct on new liquidity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight dips to 5.8/6.0 pct on new liquidity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 5.8/6.0 percent from 7.5/7 on Friday as liquidity improved on the back of a strengthening ringgit, dealers said on Monday.
They said the sharp decline was unexpected as the rate had been holding firm despite heavy inflow of overseas funds for most of last week.
The ringgit hit a 17-month high of 2.4690 a dollar on Monday morning on sustained buying by U.S. and Japanese funds.
"The overnight should have been around these levels for the last few days. The story is not about the fall today, but why was it firm for the last few days," one Malaysian dealer said.
"It is possible that those who have the funds, particularly foreign banks and big local banks, are reluctant to lend to the risky names which are in the market," the dealer said.
There were also rumours that Bank Negara was last week directly borrowing from select banks to prevent rates from falling. No confirmation was available from the central bank.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the market to keep liquidity under check or set interest rates. Sometimes it comes in to borrow directly from select banks, which are also its principal dealers.
Earlier, interbank rates in Kuala Lumpur were firmer on demand from institutions considered high risk borrowers.
Funds were also flowing in through swaps, but the liquidity was not visible in the market, the dealers said.
One-week and two-week money were steady around 7.20/40 percent.
One-month and two-month money were at 7.30/35 percent against 7.25/30, while three-month was steady at 7.35 percent. Six-month was offered at 7.40 percent.
